summary.headline: Azad Engineering Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 26.8% YoY to INR170.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 37.6% and PAT of INR36.4 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 26.8% YoY and 8.3% QoQ to INR170.5 crore, with reported EBITDA of INR64 crore (37.6% margin, up 150 bps YoY). PAT rose 21.2% YoY to INR36.4 crore (21.3% margin, EPS INR5.63), held back by other income falling to INR4 crore from INR17 crore in Q4 FY26 on forex swings. Management highlighted delivery of India's first indigenous expendable turbojet engine to GTRE/DRDO and a new Baker Hughes dedicated facility, while stating that substantial revenue from new capacity begins in H2 FY27.

segments.name: Aerospace and Defense (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth stated as 24.7% YoY after management first said ~38.4%, corrected on call; attributed to higher share of wallet with global aviation majors and early defence/propulsion deliveries.

segments.commentary: Revenue growth stated as 26.7% YoY after first being said as 21.6%, corrected on call; driven by gas turbine components and launch of new customer-dedicated lines.

guidance_outlook: Long-term annual revenue growth guidance of over 25% reiterated; Chairman said the guidance will change once the company moves to the next level.

Management says it has met Q1 guidance; manufacturing infrastructure 'running at full throttle', with substantive revenue contributions from new capacity expected from H2 FY27 and acceleration from Q3-Q4.
EBITDA margin guidance framed as 32%-35% for calculation purposes, though company has delivered above 35% consistently.
Other income expected to moderate as treasury cash is deployed into factory infrastructure.
Remaining FY26 expansion initiatives: ~80% stabilised in Q1; major remaining activities due mid-Q2 and full closure by Q3 FY27.
Working-capital targets: debtor days ~200 in H1 and 160-180 in H2 FY27; natural hedge for export receivables expected by Q4 FY27 via bill discounting.
capex_capacity: Tuniki Bollaram Industrial Park: 8 customer-dedicated plants planned; each plant said to generate INR150-180 crore revenue at full utilisation, implying ~INR1,200 crore from newer plants.

Fourth dedicated facility (7,600 sq m, for Baker Hughes) inaugurated April 2026 and commenced operations in Q1; dedicated lines already running for Mitsubishi, GE Power Systems/GE Steam Power and Siemens Energy.
Civil construction at Azad Center of Excellence remaining units to finish within FY27; machine installations in modular phases aligned to customer roadmaps.
Management estimates ~1 year of capex-driven capacity for the next couple of years; capex plans beyond FY29 are being sketched, with quantum and timing to be disclosed in the next quarter.
Hot-section facility (modelled on the Mitsubishi plant) expected to be set up in roughly 7-8 months, also usable for aviation engines.
FY26 capex was roughly INR900 crore over two years per analyst; no new capex number was given by management.
demand_pricing: Turbojet engine: first indigenous expendable turbojet engine delivered to GTRE, DRDO and MoD; next step is weapon testing expected in 4-6 weeks per management (not formally communicated), followed by certification and production scale-up. Management says volumes are unknown (2-, 3- or 4-digit) and existing capacity is fungible for 2-digit volumes.
First 20 engines produced so far; management will share costing after 5-6 engines in a row (about 8-12 weeks away).
Rolls-Royce civil aircraft engine: first batch of qualification parts expected to be delivered within the current quarter.

Cost indigenisation: local suppliers Sunflag and Star Wire qualified for critical raw-material grades; import freight of ~4-5% avoided. Raw material cost fell to ~5% of sales from ~12% a year earlier, per analyst.
Employee cost rose to ~INR42 crore from ~INR29 crore per analyst; management attributed it to inventory build for H2 sales and hiring of ~150-200 people per month into 90-day training.
Management said rupee depreciation can add roughly 5-6% to revenue but is not a planning lever; FX on exports is below EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline from first turbojet engine delivery to orders and capacity planning beyond FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said next steps are weapon testing in 4-6 weeks and then certification and production; capacity is fungible for 2-digit volumes, and capex quantum/timing for next 5-6 years will be clarified in about a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Growth thesis for aerospace hot-section and peers' margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said hot-section demand is a multi-billion market, OEMs are already asking when the facility is ready, and margin potential is referenced to high-cost-country peers; no growth number given.

qa_highlights.question: When will working capital days plateau?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO targeted ~200 debtor days in H1 and 160-180 in H2 FY27, mainly via bill discounting that will move ~170-180 day debtors toward ~90 days; finance cost will continue to rise on discounting charges.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide 32-35% EBITDA margin when delivering 37-38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 32-35% is used for guidance and calculation purposes, while margins have been running above 35% due to shop-floor skills and continuous improvement, from ~18-19% at inception.

qa_highlights.question: Is revenue growth above 25% achievable given 3-year potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 25%+ is guided given current situation and the guidance will change on moving to the next level; no 3-year target given.

qa_highlights.question: Does rupee depreciation benefit revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is natural hedging, with imports offsetting exports; CFO said FX benefit is below EBITDA and not built into the margin.

risks_watch: Turbojet engine: timing of weapon testing (said to be 4-6 weeks, not formally communicated), certification, and production volumes (2-, 3- or 4-digit) remain unconfirmed; costing to be shared only after 5-6 engines in a row (8-12 weeks).

Execution load: 80% of FY26 expansion initiatives stabilised in Q1, with remaining work due mid-Q2 and full closure by Q3 FY27; management itself flagged the complexity of building factories, ramping capacity and hiring/training simultaneously.

Working capital and finance cost: debtor days ~170-180 today versus targets of ~200 in H1 and 160-180 in H2 FY27; bill discounting will keep raising finance cost, and natural hedge for export receivables depends on discounting lines being in place by Q4 FY27.

Other income is expected to moderate as treasury cash is deployed into capex, and Q1 FY27 other income (INR4 crore) was well below Q4 FY26 (INR17 crore) on forex swings, so reported PAT growth is sensitive to FX.
Capex beyond FY29 and the quantum/timing of further capex were not quantified; management will address it next quarter. Consolidated subsidiary turnaround targets were not specified.

Revenue growth from new capacity is back-ended to H2 FY27 and Q3-Q4; Q1 sequential growth (8.3%) is the only near-term datapoint, and peer growth comparisons were dismissed by management without a quantified response.
key_quotes: We proudly reiterate our long -term annual revenue growth guidance of over 25%, while maintaining our stellar industry-leading profitability profile.
But for calculation purpose and for the guidance purpose, I think 32%, 35% is a good number, which we are holding for since long.
So we are doing our math internally to figure out what is the capital -- how much is the quantum of capital do we need and when do we actually need that.
Entirely, it will be hedged by quarter 4 type of time once we have all the bill discounting facility in place.
summary.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional on the turbojet engine, capacity and long-term growth, with the Chairman and WTD repeatedly stressing "no hiccups". Evasive on specifics: volumes, engine costing, capex quantum, Rolls-Royce timing and pipeline details were deferred to "next quarter" or "a meeting in person", and several numbers (consolidated revenue, segment growth) were corrected on the call.

growth.why: Management reiterates long-term revenue growth above 25% for FY27 and beyond, with substantive contribution from new capacity (8 planned Tuniki Bollaram plants, ~INR1,200 crore implied) expected only from H2 FY27, while Q1 revenue grew 26.8% YoY and EBITDA 32.1%.
